$comment: Canonical taxonomy of event-driven source categories required by Constitution Amendment 2. This dictionary describes the SHAPE an implementation must satisfy; it does NOT describe any particular implementation. Any conforming implementation of the Compliance-to-Architecture Framework must declare its own event sources against these categories and prove (via an event registry of its own) that none of them is post-facto.

amendment.description: End-to-end latency from real-world event to first observable consumer must not exceed 30 seconds. Cron-only ingestion is forbidden as a PRIMARY trigger. A safety-net cron is permitted only when (a) a primary event trigger exists, and (b) the cron is documented as belt-and-suspenders, not the primary path. Documentation, indexing, reconciliation, audit-trail and verdict pipelines are all in-scope.

phases.$comment: Constitution Amendment 1 — 5-phase lifecycle. Every event must carry its phase tag.
phases.upstream: Change requested but not yet committed (intent declared).
phases.midstream: Mutation in flight (engine running, deploy uploading, payment authorising).
phases.downstream: Mutation committed (verdict written, deploy live, payment captured).
phases.propagation: Downstream consumers notified (cache invalidated, webhook fired, customer emailed).
phases.compensating: Failure / rollback (chargeback, deploy rolled back, drift remediated).

categories.name: Regulatory framework updates
categories.$note: The fallback is intentionally relaxed for this category — most regulators do not expose machine-readable change webhooks; a daily safety-net is the practical floor today.

categories.name: Customer cloud events (for the implementation that consumes them)
categories.$note: Cross-cloud implementations MUST use the customer's own native event bus, never poll their API on a schedule. Polling violates Amendment 2 and the BYOC-vault contract.

requirementsForConformingImplementations: Maintain a private event registry that lists every source the implementation owns, mapped to a category in this dictionary.
For each source, declare: primaryTrigger, fallbackTrigger, maxLatencyMs, phases emitted, consumers.
Gate CI on the registry: any source with status='violation' past its fix-by date fails the build.
Publish a digest of the registry's status (counts of compliant / in-flight / violation) so an auditor can verify Amendment 2 conformance without seeing the implementation details.

complianceProofSchema.$comment: Reference shape an implementation publishes to prove Amendment 2 conformance. Implementations expose this at /v1/event-registry/digest or equivalent.
complianceProofSchema.violationFixByDate: ISO-8601 date — must be in the future when violationCount > 0
complianceProofSchema.categoryBreakdown: Record<categoryId, {compliant: int, inFlight: int, violation: int}>
